transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-19 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood CSM), Carlos (Redwood SE), Dr. Aisha Khan (Hearthline CTO), Liam O'Connor (IT Ops), Priya Rao (Security), Marcus Bell (Product), Nicole (Procurement)

Summary / Goals (auto-gen, may be rough):
- Align on security/compliance prerequisites for Pilot (HIPAA).
- Decide on deployment mode preferences (private control plane / VPC).
- Identify stakeholders and timelines for 6-week pilot.

Transcript: (timestamps approximate, auto-transcribed)
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone, welcome, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the AE on this account. We've got Maya CSM and Carlos our SE.
[00:08] Dr. Aisha: Hi thanks, appreciate you all. Quick context — Hearthline is launching a clinical triage assistant and uptime/latency and HIPAA compliance are the blockers for us.
[00:17] Maya: Great, that helps frame it. Today we'd like to walk through activation steps, security checklist, and propose a pilot runway.
[00:25] Liam: Quick note — IT wants VPC-only traffic, we can't allow model telemetry leaving our VPC unless it's encrypted and logged, so network story is important.
[00:33] Jordan: Understood. For that we usually offer Private deployment with private control plane — customer-managed VPC peering and optional on-prem connector. Carlos, want to take the technical run?
[00:41] Carlos: Sure. High level, there are three common modes: Hosted (fastest, but not ideal for PHI), Dedicated (reserved GPU capacity in Redwood's infra with tenant isolation), and Private (control plane in your VPC or on-prem). For HIPAA and data residency you tend to want Private or Dedicated with VPC peering and strict KMS/HSM integration.
[00:57] Priya: For us, the main requirements are: encrypted-at-rest with customer KMS, audit logs forwarded to our SIEM, SSO (SAML) integration for RBAC, and data retention controls. Also need to know where the model weights are kept during inference.
[01:14] Carlos: Good questions. Model weights live on the serving nodes; in Private deployment the nodes are in your VPC or on-prem so weights do not leave your environment. In Dedicated the nodes are in Redwood's environment but we can provide contract-backed data isolation and options for disk encryption with customer-managed keys.
[01:32] Dr. Aisha: Disk encryption with CMK is required. Also, do you have SOC2 type II reports and penetration test summaries we can share with our compliance team?
[01:42] Jordan: Yes, we'll share SOC2 and our latest pen test summary in the security pack. I'll include the contact for our compliance team.
[01:48] Nicole: Procurement will need a high-level SOW and pricing tiers — pilot pricing vs committed Dedicated.
[01:53] Jordan: We'll include that. Maya will outline recommended pilot SKUs and a commit vs usage sheet.
[01:58] [02:05] Maya: Pilot proposal — 6 weeks, start in staging with canary traffic, ramp to 5k qps peak? (note: numbers tentative) We'll run a controlled sample of triage requests, capture latency and cost. Success metrics: P95 latency < 250ms for short prompts, error rate < 0.5%, and no PII leakage in logs.
[02:23] Marcus: For product we'd like to measure false positives on triage suggestions, and overall satisfaction compared to human baseline. We'll share evaluation prompts.
[02:31] Carlos: From SE side, we'll provide a benchmark harness (script) for you to run from within your VPC to validate latencies. We'll instrument KV cache and prefix caching — note, transcription sometimes reads that as K-V cash — but it's KV cache that speeds subsequent token calls.
[02:48] Liam: On networking, we need a permanent peering and a short-lived tunnel for initial tests — firewall rules will only allow traffic to Redwood's dedicated egress IPs, we'll provide those once we have the list.
[02:57] Jordan: We'll give an IP list and ports. Also, if you prefer on-prem HW we can also discuss appliance-based Private.
[03:05] Dr. Aisha: Not likely on-prem for now. Important: HSM/KMS integration. How does Redwood integrate with client KMS?
[03:12] Carlos: We support client-managed KMS for disk and at-rest encryption. For key usage during runtime we can integrate with your KMS using transient keys and audit every key usage. We'll include the KMS integration doc.
[03:24] Priya: Also need audit log format to consume into Splunk — can you push logs to S3 with a prefix we pick or push via syslog?
[03:31] Maya: We support S3 log delivery and SIEM forwarding. We'll capture request-level metadata (request id, model, route, timestamp) — we'll provide schema.
[03:40] [03:47] Nicole: On timeline — Procurement needs 30 day lead to finalize contracts after receiving the SOW.
[03:52] Jordan: We'll aim to have the SOW and pricing in 2 business days.
[03:55] Liam: For the pilot, we need to know expected token costs and also how batching works — we need deterministic latency for triage use.
[04:04] Carlos: Batching can reduce cost but may increase tail latency. We recommend request-level routing for triage with small batch windows (10-30ms) or dynamic batching based on QPS. For strict P95 SLOs, Dedicated with tuned batching and prefix caching is typical.
[04:20] Dr. Aisha: Is there a plan for model fallbacks if capacity is low? We need reliability guarantees.
[04:26] Jordan: Yes, we can set routing policies: primary model (optimized for latency), fallback model (lower-cost) and region failover. For mission-critical, we can reserve capacity in Dedicated.
[04:36] [04:45] Marcus: We might test a 2-model approach: small specialist model for triage + larger for complex follow-ups, with automatic routing.
[04:53] Carlos: That works; we can show routing policy examples in the playbook.
[04:58] Jordan: Ok quick recap — action items and timeline. We'll circle back on the exact pilot configuration. Carlos, you'll draft the benchmark script. Maya will compile the security pack. Jordan will send SOW and pricing. Customer will send network diagram and retention needs.
[05:12] Dr. Aisha: Sounds good. A couple of minor clarifications: do you retain prompts for model improvement? We need strict opt-in.
[05:20] Maya: By default, hosted research opt-in is off for enterprise customers; for Private/Dedicated you control retention. We'll document retention options.
[05:29] Priya: Also please include a sample SLAs addendum for PHI-handling.
[05:34] Jordan: We'll include a compliance addendum template.
[05:37] [05:45] Nicole: Next, procurement will want a standard IP indemnity and data processing agreement. Is that something Redwood has in a template?
[05:52] Jordan: Yes, we have a DPA and an enterprise agreement template; i'll attach them.
[05:56] Liam: Technical Q: does Redwood support VPC endpoints via PrivateLink or just peering?
[06:02] Carlos: We support VPC peering and PrivateLink in select regions — we'll confirm region support. We'll call that out in the runbook.
[06:10] Marcus: For product, team will prepare eval prompts and failure cases. We'll share a spreadsheet.
[06:16] Jordan: Great. Anything else?
[06:20] Dr. Aisha: One last thing — can we do an initial performance run with synthetic traffic that mimics our triage payloads?
[06:27] Carlos: Absolutely. We'll provide the harness and help with the scripts. Expect a short tuning cycle.
[06:33] [06:40] Maya: Ok wrap-up — I'll send a short recap email and the security pack by Friday (2027-01-21). Let's schedule the tunnel+ops session for week of Jan 24.
[06:50] Jordan: Thanks everyone. We'll get the SOW and pricing and loop in legal where needed.
[06:55] Dr. Aisha: Thank you, appreciate the clarity.
[07:00] (calls ends)

Notes on transcription quality: medium — some technical terms were mistranscribed (e.g., KV cache -> K-V cash) and speaker boundaries occasionally overlapped.
